messages:
maya: heads-up — noticed a flurry of failover hits for eu-west when canarying v2. routing policy shows prefer-local then cost-fallback but traffic jumped regions for a tiny latency blip.
liam: ah, saw that too. looks like header overrides might be bypassing geo affinity sticky cookie. can you paste the route rule?
maya: here’s the rule snippet we pushed in the canary:
```
match: path.startsWith('/api/v2')
policies:
  - name: geo_affinity
    params:
      prefer_local: true
      stickiness_header: 'x-rr-geo'
  - name: cost_fallback
    params:
      threshold_ms: 250
      fallback_regions: ['eu-west', 'us-west']
  - name: header_overrides
    params:
      header: 'X-Redwood-Prefer'
      precedence: high
```
maya: note: we also set a quota-based routing rule on the tenant that directs excess to a cheaper pool in us-west. :grimacing:
samir: that header_overrides/precedence: high is suspicious — if incoming requests set X-Redwood-Prefer=us-west the header should win. but why would a tiny latency spike cause headers to be respected over stickiness?
tess: remember stickiness is implemented as a soft hint unless we set strict_affinity: true. default was soft. small blips can trigger failover circuit which then re-evaluates policies and header overrides may take precedence.
liam: ok that explains the behavior. two asks: 1) can we make stickiness strict for rollout sessions? 2) add telemetry counters for policy-evaluations and policy-decisions in the dashboard so we can see which policy caused the region change.
maya: +1 to both. for (1) is strict_affinity opt-in per-route? where does UX expose it?
samir: currently param exists in config but console treats it as advanced (hidden). I can flip it on for the canary routes but worried about long-term implications (sticky sessions may hurt failover recovery).
nora: from an ops POV we need a tiebreaker ordering so header overrides are applied before cost fallbacks only when explicitly allowed. propose adding a precedence array: [stickiness, header_overrides, latency, cost_fallback] so it's deterministic.
tess: love the precedence array idea. Also suggest adding a latency hysteresis window (e.g., require > threshold for N seconds) to avoid jitter-based ejections.
liam: +1 on hysteresis. And add a metric: policy_evaluation.reason = {stickiness,header,latency,cost} emitted on each region decision so dashboards can be filtered.
maya: can we also get a small preview tool in console: given a sample request headers + ip it shows the final routing decision and which policy matched? would help on-rollout debugging.
samir: we have a PR draft for a route-preview CLI but not hooked into console. I'll push a prototype and wire an API endpoint for it.
deploy-bot: deploy status — route config v2-canary pushed to staging at 2026-03-16T14:22:11Z (sha: bd9a4f).
liam: follow-up: I increased stickiness to strict for the canary and added hysteresis=10s. monitor dashboards for new policy_evaluation metric.
maya: thanks — watching now. If we still see mismatches I'll open an incident. :thumbsup:
nora: long-term: we should document fallback prioritization and add a UX toggle: "Respect client-preferred-region" with explicit risk text. fewer surprises that way.
liam: agreed. will file a console UX ticket and link to this thread.
maya: filing ticket would be great. tagging @samir @tess for followups on telemetry and preview tool.
samir: got it — I'll add the metric, push the preview endpoint, and prototype precedence array in the config schema.
liam: baseline check — does anyone object to making precedence explicit (rather than implicit ordering)?
tess: no objections. it's safer and debuggable.
maya: cool. closing the loop here. thanks y'all.
